roles.title: Président de la République

holder_claims.name: François Mitterrand
holder_claims.note: Observed on 4 January 1990, the first in-text attestation in the period: at their joint press conference at Latché (Élysée archive transcript) Chancellor Kohl says 'Je suis d'accord avec M. Mitterrand' and speaks of working in 1990 with 'le Président de la République'. The Assemblée nationale's record of 27 August 1990 reads his decree of 22 August 1990 and his message of 27 August 1990, both signed FRANÇOIS MITTERRAND.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: his second septennat began before the packet period; decision 88-60 PDR of 11 May 1988 ('prendra effet le 21 mai 1988 à 0 heure') and his investiture address of 21 May 1988 are claims on the role, not a holder date, as the Brazil, India and South Africa packets date the holder in office when the period opens by an in-period attestation. No end: no source reviewed states, as a record, the day his functions ended. His letter of 16 May 1995 announces the handover for 'Demain matin à onze heures' (prospective), decision 95-81 PDR gives only the outer limit of 21 May 1995 at 0 heure, his successor's address of 17 May 1995 speaks of the fourteen years 'qui viennent de s'écouler' without a day, and the Council's undated 2012 note dating the 1995 handover to 17 May is retrospective; all are claims, and Jacques Chirac's observation of 17 May 1995 is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Jacques Chirac
holder_claims.note: Observed on 17 May 1995: in his address at the Élysée dated that day he says 'En ce jour où je prends la responsabilité d'assumer la plus haute charge de l'Etat', and in his message to the armed forces of the same day he writes 'Président de la République, c'est en tant que chef des Armées que je m'adresse à vous' (Élysée archive).

roles.scope_note: Président de la République under the Constitution of 4 October 1958, recorded as head of state. CLAUDE-C01-23 keeps each election round, the Constitutional Council's declaration of first-round results, its proclamation of the result and the President of the Council's oral announcement of it, the proclamation's publication in the Journal officiel, the handover meeting, the investiture ceremony, a stated start of term, the outer limit the Council states for the predecessor's cessation, the holder's own statements and announcements and his in-office acts as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where the Constitutional Council, in its decision or in its President's address at the investiture, states the day the mandate takes effect or office is taken up, and an end only where a source states the day the office ended; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. A start before the packet period (1 January 1990) is not structured: the holder in office when the period opens is dated by attested_on. The holder's own statement that he assumes office that day supports but never makes a start; a prospective announcement of a handover, an outer limit ('au plus tard'), a successor's statement, a computed expiry and a successor's start are never ends. Retrospective notes, reports, tables and timelines are claims only, and table rows and timeline entries carry no structured date. Élysée archive headings are later catalogue labels. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. No interim presidency (Article 7) is stated for 1990-2026, so none is recorded; acting or interim service would be a claim only, never a holder. Prime ministers, ministers and party offices are outside this role.

unresolved: Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-23, FR-PRES-01..10) are dated holder observations from the Constitutional Council's decisions, communications and investiture addresses, the Journal officiel (archived Légifrance text pages and DILA open-data exports), the Assemblée nationale's debates and the Élysée's archive. François Mitterrand is dated by attested_on (4 January 1990); the effect day of 21 May 1988 that decision 88-60 PDR states lies before the period and is a claim only. Stated starts: 17 May 2002 (Jacques Chirac), 16 May 2007 (Nicolas Sarkozy), 15 May 2012 (François Hollande), and 14 May 2017 and 14 May 2022 (Emmanuel Macron). Jacques Chirac's 1995 term is dated only by attested_on (17 May 1995): no decision or address of the President of the Council fixes its first day.

No source reviewed states, as a record of the event, the day any President's functions ended, so no holder has an until. The Council states only outer limits ('au plus tard') for 1995, 2007, 2012 and 2017; François Mitterrand (16 May 1995), Jacques Chirac (15 May 2007) and François Hollande (10 May 2017) announced their handovers in advance; the Council's undated 2012 note, its 2017 dossier and activity report and the Élysée's biography timeline are retrospective.

Hours: the Council explicitly fixes the 2002 and 2022 term effects at '0 heure'; the 1988 decision likewise fixes midnight before this packet's period. No exact assumption-of-office hour is established here for 2007, 2012 and 2017. The Council's 2007 page puts the investiture ceremony at 11:00, while the Élysée puts the outgoing President's reception of his successor at 11:00 before it. Holder dates remain day-granular, with explicit times preserved in the claims.

Not retrieved: the Journal officiel publications of the 1988, 1995 and 2002 proclamations (Légifrance refuses automated access and no capture was found), and the published correction (rectificatif) of the 2007 proclamation, JORFTEXT000000465545, whose content could not be read; the Council's 2017 dossier reprints the 2007 dispositif with the same dates.

No interim presidency (Article 7 of the Constitution) is stated for 1 January 1990 to the 7 September 2026 cutoff, so none is recorded; this records the absence of such a statement in the sources reviewed, not a proven absence. Keep executive office distinct from party leadership and from the CNCCFP financial-reporting identities: no organization in this packet is mapped to this institution.

roles.scope_note: Premier ministre under the Constitution of 4 October 1958 (article 8), recorded as head of government. CLAUDE-C01-37 keeps the Prime Minister's letter presenting the Government's resignation, the President's decree ending the Government's functions, the President's decree appointing a Prime Minister, a decree the Prime Minister signs or countersigns and a later decree's reference to an appointment as separate dated claims. Head-of-government source observations under fr_pm, distinct from the presidency and party offices. Four signatures/countersignatures attest the named Prime Minister in office on their dates; twelve appointment instruments provide dated named appointment observations. Each attested_on identifies its first cited source event, not an effective term boundary. All reviewed from/until values remain unknown: no separate explicit effective-date support was established. Fourteen cessation instruments and the dated resignation letters they cite remain separate claims. No continuity, acting service or absence of current-affairs continuation is inferred.
